analysis.summary: This is a simple Express.js application providing user authentication (register, login) and profile retrieval, along with a health check endpoint. It uses an in-memory Map for storing user data, bcryptjs for password hashing, and jsonwebtoken for session tokens.
components: app.js: Entry point for the Express application. Sets up middleware, health check route, and mounts the users router under /users.
routes/users.js: User routes handling registration, login, and profile lookup by email using an in-memory Map.
risks: routes/users.js line 7: In-memory Map used for user storage (const users = new Map()). State will not persist across restarts or scale across multiple worker processes in FastAPI/Uvicorn.
routes/users.js line 28: Relies on process.env.JWT_SECRET without a fallback or validation check.

steps.title: Create users router
steps.description: Create routers/users.py with APIRouter(prefix="/users"), handling POST /users/register, POST /users/login, and GET /users/{email} using bcrypt and PyJWT.
steps.notes: Migrated users router from Express.js to FastAPI using APIRouter, Pydantic models for request validation, bcrypt, and PyJWT. In-memory Map was replaced with a standard dictionary.

steps.title: Create main application
steps.description: Create main.py with FastAPI(), the GET /health route, and include the users router.
steps.notes: Created main.py with FastAPI app instance, health check endpoint, and included the users router.
